verdicts.reason: Opened all four cites. REBUILD_READINESS.md:165 reads verbatim '("dan rank 5 (kyudan)" - kyudan=9th); film shows a **flat +25 gold** every rebirth, no 10th-rebirth tier.' and :205 reads verbatim '(5) rebirth/element-picker UI (never filmed - both longplays pre-rebirth).' The ledger does contradict itself: :205 says the rebirth screen was never on camera, so :165's 'film shows' provenance cannot stand. The value is banked at :79-80 ('rebirth scroll 1000c (+25g)') and is confirmed by shipped WEB code - payload/§1t1523s0§.as:2651 'changeStat(HGOLD,25)' in the else arm, with :2644-2646 paying 100 at Dan 8. The 'no 10th-rebirth tier' half is therefore false as well. Re-tag A2/code-sourced, exactly as filed.

Every quoted line is verbatim. Web §1t99s0§.as:3284-3290 is 'internal function §1t4477s0§() : int { if(this.stance == §1t12222s0§) { return defense * 0.8; } return defense; }' and '_loc5_ -= this.§1t4477s0§();' appears at :3484, :3800 AND :4391. I independently confirmed §1t12222s0§ is Heavy: §1t99s0§.as:31 'internal static var §1t12222s0§:int = 2' against android MCSPlayer.as:31 'HEAVY_STANCE:int = 2'. Android twin verbatim at MCSPlayer.as:3231-3238 and :3415 'damage -= this.getDefense();'. Mitigation is flat subtraction with a min-damage floor; there is no curve to measure, so RR:200 blocker (1)'s DEF half closes.

Opened §1t401s0§.as:1050-1095. Every quoted line is character-exact: :1058 'cost = §1t1525s0§.§1t9936s0§() * 10;', :1068 the null/0/13000 refusal, :1076 'changeGold(-cost)', :1077-1080 'if(weapon.uses > 1) { weapon.uses = 1; }', :1081 achievement 60005, :1087 'cost = 5000;'. StatsManager.as:1854-1860 is verbatim: 'internal static function getSkillCooldownModifierVal(speed:int) : Number { if(speed > 300) { speed = 300; } return 1 - speed / 300 * 0.5; }'. Consumed verbatim at InventoryUI.as:1937 and printed at :2233 ('skill cooldown modifier: ... 0.' + int(mod*1000)). The formula IS recovered and RR:195 (4) closes. The finding was honest that web parity was unchecked; I checked it and it DIVERGES - the web twin is §1t1523s0§.as:2289-2295, 'if(param1 > 600) param1 = 600; return 1 - param1 / 600 * 0.5;', fed from stat §1t9410s0§ = 8 (STAT_SPEED) at :2279-2286 with the same *= 1.5 buff branch. Held as filed for v0.682; see NF-D before any promotion to CONTRACT. Its lane_impact aside ('back-solves to SPD 150') is android-only arithmetic - under the web curve 0.75 back-solves to SPD 300.

I recomputed the whole join from scratch rather than trusting the number. 121_Mobile_PremiumData.bin yields 143 unique <item> ids; joining them to itemdata.xml <heavenlyprice> gives exactly {'1': 20, '2': 2, '3': 94, '5': 4, '12': 23} with zero ids missing from itemdata. CORRECTION to the finding's build field: it says 'prices WEB itemdata.xml', but under C2 reference/extracted/itemdata.xml IS the android blob (184,002 B vs 111_Mobile_ItemData.bin 184,044 B - the 42-byte decl+CRLF delta I measured). Parsed skilldata.xml myself: skills 1000, 1001 and 1002 each contain exactly 10 <level> blocks with <value> 1..10. Skill 1002's <desc>6005</desc> resolves to strings.json['6005'] 'Slow but powerful stance... Defense -20%', pinning 1002 = Heavy and the mapping of the other two. So the published table is the mastery-10 row and RR:155's 'MASTERY-9 CEILING' label is off by one; RR:157's 'target mastery-9' advice would ship the wrong numbers. verdicts.reason: REFUTED on the identity claim. I parsed BOTH blobs. The finding's four aggregates are correct - 39 <wave>, 87 <enemy>, x histogram {-50:49, 1650:37, -1650:1} in each - but they are invariant under the actual edit and the files are NOT identical. Sizes differ: web bindata/119_1t4646s0.bin 11,721 B vs android 109_WarHexUI_SurvivalModeData.bin 11,553 B, and 14 of the 87 enemy rows differ. Web rows 73-84 read '449|454|449|454|443', '450|455|450|455|443', '451|456|451|456|443' where android reads '449|454', '450|455', '451|456' - the web build adds enemy 443 to three late-wave alternation pools. The unique-id sets are unequal in both directions. 'byte-identical', 'authored content is IDENTICAL' and 'Every figure matches ... exactly' are all false, and the proposed upgrade from 'android v0.682' to 'both' does not follow. What survives: survival mode IS present in the web payload with 39 authored waves, so S0-1's gap can be specified from the target build. Re-filed as NF-E.

EnemyShield.as:39 'var finishedAnimation:String = mcs.updateAnimation();' and :123-125 '--gotHitCounter' are BOTH inside 'override public function update()' (opens :25, closes :127) - one animation advance and one counter decrement per update, so genuinely the same clock. REFUTED: the lines are real, two of the six mechanics built from them are not what the code does. (a) 'It recharges +6 per tick' is FALSE. The per-tick fill is MCSPlayer.as:1158-1160 'if(this.reload < this.maxreload) { ++this.reload; }' = +1/tick. The +6 at :3267 is inside bonusReload(), whose only call site in the entire android bundle is NPCManager.as:1709-1711 'if(deathCount > 0) { StatsManager.getPlayer().bonusReload(); }' - a per-enemy-KILL bonus. My full census of every write to reload in MCSPlayer.as (:240, :1160, :3100, :3108, :3244, :3261, :3267) shows no other fill path. A Sim built from this finding fills Focus 6x too fast. (b) 'is penalised on being hit (reload > max/2 collapses to max/3, else -max/6)' is FALSE: :3098-3104 sits inside 'public function setStance(num:int)' which opens at :3019 - it is the STANCE-SWITCH cost, i.e. exactly the thing RR:195 (3) asks for, mislabelled as an on-hit penalty. The remaining mechanics (maxreload 5*24, gate at max/6, per-stance slash drain, crit at full, zero-on-crit, BattleUI scaleX/crittext) are verbatim correct. RR:190 (5) does not close on these values; NF-B and NF-C carry the corrected closure plus the WEB constants the finding rightly flagged as unchecked.

All four string lookups are verbatim in docs/gauntlet/L0/index/strings.json: ['8131'] 'Light Stance Mastery Level 10.', ['8132'] 'Balanced Stance Mastery Level 10.', ['8133'] 'Heavy Stance Mastery Level 10.', ['6005'] 'Slow but powerful stance. Damage inflicted is increased but slash range is shorter.\nEffective against Balanced Stance.\nDefense -20%'. MCSPlayer.as:3701-3703 is verbatim, and the ordering claim is exactly right: the x1.2 lands BEFORE ':3709 damage -= this.getDefense();', before the ':3710-3713' min-damage floor, and before ':3714-3716 if(behead) damage *= 1.5;'. Every one of its nine cite anchors resolves verbatim (:3094, :3105, :3116-3119, :3131, :3142-3145, :3158, :183-199, and §1t1523s0§.as:2344-2347). Its closing warning - that combat tuning is exactly where v0.682 and v0.717 drift - is confirmed four more times in this review (NF-A, NF-B, NF-D, NF-E).

new_findings.text: The stance counter-triangle has TWO arms in web v0.717, not one. Winning matchups (Light vs Balanced, Balanced vs Heavy, Heavy vs Light) take damage x1.2; LOSING matchups (Light vs Heavy, Balanced vs Light, Heavy vs Balanced) take damage x0.9. Android v0.682 has only the x1.2 arm - grep for '*= 0.9' across MCSPlayer.as returns zero hits. Both arms are applied before the defense subtraction and before the min-damage floor. REBUILD_READINESS.md:74 carries neither term; a Sim written from that bullet is wrong by 20% on countered matchups and by 10% on countering ones.
new_findings.ledger_text: **Damage math:** Physical = (ATK + WeaponDMG) × stanceMult; Heavy defender Defense ×0.8 (one way);
new_findings.lane_impact: L1/L5 combat-core: RR:74 needs both triangle arms added, and the pair must be applied pre-defense, pre-floor.

new_findings.text: The Focus/reload model differs between builds on four constants, and the web values are the ones a v0.717 target needs. maxreload is 8*24 = 192 in web (§1t99s0§.as:249) against 5*24 = 120 in android (MCSPlayer.as:239). The stance-switch cost is a FLAT -48 in web (§1t99s0§.as:3162-3165) against 'reload > max/2 -> max/3, else -= max/6' in android (MCSPlayer.as:3098-3105). The stance-switch gate is 'reload >= 48' in web (§1t99s0§.as:3050 and :3060) against 'reload < max/6' in android (MCSPlayer.as:2977). The HUD normalisation is (reload-48)/(max-48) in web (§1t113s0§.as:326-328) against (reload-24)/(max-24) in android (MCSPlayer.as:3272). Unchanged across builds: +1 fill per tick, the per-stance slash drain (x0.5 light / x1 balanced+reversed / x1.5 heavy+dual), zero-on-crit-slash, and the +6 kill bonus. This closes RR:195 (3) 'Focus numerics (max/fill/switch-cost)' and RR:190 (5) on WEB constants.

new_findings.lane_impact: L2 skills-meters + L5 combat-core: the blocker closes, but only on the WEB constants. Porting the android Focus model to a v0.717 target is wrong on max, switch-cost, gate and HUD scale simultaneously.

new_findings.text: The Focus meter fills +1 per tick, not +6. In android the per-tick fill is 'if(this.reload < this.maxreload) { ++this.reload; }' (MCSPlayer.as:1158-1160) and the web twin is identical (§1t99s0§.as:1203-1205). The +6 lives in bonusReload() (MCSPlayer.as:3265-3272; web twin §1t99s0§.as:3318-3325), whose only call site in the entire android bundle is NPCManager.as:1709-1711 'if(deathCount > 0) { StatsManager.getPlayer().bonusReload(); }' - i.e. a bonus granted once per batch of enemy deaths, not a tick rate. A full census of every write to reload in MCSPlayer.as (:240, :1160, :3100, :3108, :3244, :3261, :3267) shows no other fill path. Combined with NF-B's maxreload, the web bar takes 192 ticks (8 s at 24 fps) to fill from empty with no kills.

new_findings.text: The web v0.717 SPEED-to-skill-cooldown transfer function saturates at SPD 600, not SPD 300: cooldownModifier = 1 - min(speed, 600) / 600 * 0.5. The shape is the same linear halving as android's, but the knee is at twice the speed, so at any given SPD below 300 the web build gives HALF the cooldown reduction the android formula does (e.g. SPD 150 -> 0.875 web vs 0.75 android). The wrapper is the structural twin of android getSkillCooldownModifier: it reads stat §1t9410s0§ = 8 (= STAT_SPEED, android StatsManager.as:186) and applies the same *= 1.5 buff branch before delegating.

Both hold 39 <wave> and 87 <enemy> rows with the same spawn-x histogram {-50: 49, 1650: 37, -1650: 1}, but 14 of the 87 enemy rows differ: web rows 73-76 read id '449|454|449|454|443' where android reads '449|454', rows 77-80 read '450|455|450|455|443' vs '450|455', and rows 81-84 read '451|456|451|456|443' vs '451|456'. The web build adds enemy 443 to three late-wave alternation pools. The unique-id sets are unequal in both directions. Survival mode IS in the target build and can be specified from it - but from the WEB blob, not the android one.
